sentences.text: Harriotta is a genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Rhinochimaeridae within the class Chondrichthyes.
Living members of this genus are commonly known as rabbitfish, spookfish, or chimaera.
The genus currently includes three species: Harriotta avia, Harriotta haeckeli, and Harriotta raleighana.
Harriotta lehmani was described by Werdelin in 1986 from fossils found in Lebanon dating to the Late Cretaceous.
Harriotta gosseleti was described by Winkler in 1880 from fossils found in Belgium dating to the Oligocene.
Harriotta avia was described by Finucci, Didier, Ebert, Green, and Kemper in 2024.
The Paleobiology Database records two fossil occurrences for the genus Harriotta.
Modern species inhabit deep waters of continental slopes between 380 and 2,600 meters deep in the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans.
Fossil evidence for the genus dates from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
